questions.text: In an end-to-end fine-tuned LLM system, what is the correct order of the pipeline stages?
options: Deployment → Fine-tuning → Data collection → Evaluation
Data collection → Preprocessing → Fine-tuning → Evaluation → Deployment
Fine-tuning → Data collection → Deployment → Preprocessing
Evaluation → Deployment → Fine-tuning → Data collection
questions.explanation: A proper pipeline starts with gathering and cleaning data, then fine-tuning the model, evaluating its quality, and finally deploying it for inference.

questions.text: Why is evaluation on a held-out test set critical before deploying a fine-tuned model?
options: It reduces the model’s parameter count
It speeds up inference at deployment time
It automatically fixes any bugs in the model
It reveals whether the model generalizes beyond the training data and catches overfitting
questions.explanation: A held-out test set was never seen during training, so performance on it indicates real-world generalization. Poor test performance signals overfitting or data issues that must be addressed before deployment.

questions.text: What role does data preprocessing play in a fine-tuning pipeline?
options: It cleans, formats, and structures raw data into the format the model expects for training
It replaces the model’s tokenizer with a new one
It increases the model’s context window automatically
It deploys the model to a production server
questions.explanation: Preprocessing transforms raw collected data into clean, properly formatted training examples (e.g., instruction-response pairs, chat format) that the fine-tuning script expects.

questions.text: Which components are typically part of a complete fine-tuned LLM deployment?Select all that apply
options: A dedicated pretraining cluster running 24/7
An inference server with the fine-tuned model loaded and an API endpoint
Monitoring and logging to track model performance in production
A manual copy-paste workflow for each user request
questions.explanation: A production deployment needs an inference server exposing an API, plus monitoring and logging to detect quality regressions, latency issues, or unexpected inputs. Pretraining clusters are not part of deployment.

questions.text: What is the benefit of combining fine-tuning with RAG in a capstone system?
options: It eliminates the need for any training data
It makes the model smaller and faster to load
Fine-tuning adapts the model’s style and domain knowledge, while RAG provides access to current external information
It removes the need for a context window
questions.explanation: Fine-tuning bakes domain expertise and output style into the model weights, while RAG dynamically retrieves up-to-date facts at query time. Together they produce a system that is both domain-expert and factually grounded.
